evidence.ACL: Mild laxity of ACL with increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of mucoid degeneration.
evidence.MCL: medial & lateral collateral ligaments and PCL appear to be within normal.
evidence.Medial Meniscus: Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration.
evidence.Medial OA: medial femoral condyle (grade 3-4 chondromalacia) and posterior medial plateau and some spur formation, reflecting osteoarthritis.
evidence.Lateral OA: Mild fraying articular cartilage of lateral femorotibial joint, reflecting grade 2 chondromalacia of lateral femoral conydle and grade 2-3 chondromalacia of posterior lateral tibial plateau.
evidence.PF OA: Multifocal wearing of articular cartilage of left knee, more severe at femoral trochlea ( grade 4 chondromalacia)
evidence.Synovitis: hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
evidence.Baker's: A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst.
evidence.Contusion: no significant subchondral edema or cystic change over left knee
evidence.Fracture: Old Osgood-Schlatter disease of left knee
